messages:
maria: Escalation from Acme — they hit intermittent 500s + high tail latency on embeddings. Customer gave request_id: 8d9f3c2a-4b1e-11ee-8f8f-0242ac120002. Can someone quickly search server logs?
jon: Which region/model?
maria: us-west-2, model: redwood-embed-3-large. They reported around 2026-03-10T15:12:07Z.
sam: Quick Loki/ES query to try:
```
{app="model-server"} | logfmt | request_id="8d9f3c2a-4b1e-11ee-8f8f-0242ac120002"
```
Also check ingress/nginx for upstream 502/504s around that time.
jon: note on retention: hot logs (Loki) are 14d, archived to s3 for 90d. If it's within 90d we can fetch archive objects, otherwise need to ask S3 retrieval.
maria: customer wants repro steps — they supplied a curl that timed out, here: 
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-3-large","input":["text"]}' --max-time 10
```
sam: That curl looks fine; suggest asking them to include `X-Request-Id: <uuid>` header next time so we can match quicker. Also run with `--trace-ascii` for request-level details.
ingest-bot: log-archive job completed for 2026-03-10 23:59 UTC (objects placed in s3://redwood-logs-prod/us-west-2/archives/2026-03-10/)
jon: I pulled the archive object and grepped for the request id. Found these snippets — looks like KV cache miss + a model-server 502: 
```
2026-03-10T15:12:07.123Z model-server INFO request_id=8d9f3c2a-4b1e-11ee-8f8f-0242ac120002 route=/v1/embeddings kv_cache=miss seq_len=128
2026-03-10T15:12:07.789Z model-server ERROR request_id=8d9f3c2a-4b1e-11ee-8f8f-0242ac120002 upstream_status=502 upstream_msg="worker OOM"
2026-03-10T15:12:08.012Z nginx WARN request_id=8d9f3c2a-4b1e-11ee-8f8f-0242ac120002 client=1.2.3.4 status=502
```
sam: Looks like the model host OOMed during that request. Could be a skewed batch or a quantization path edge-case. I'll open a runtime ticket and attach these lines.
lisa: I'll reply to customer with what we found and ask for a debug bundle + the curl with `X-Request-Id` and `--trace-ascii`. Also ask them to attach the exact timestamp and whether they retried.
maria: Please confirm our retention and retrieval SLA for support reply.
jon: Confirmed: hot queryable logs 14d, archived accessible 90d. S3 restore (if object moved to Glacier for >90d or deep archive) requires retrieval request ~12-48h and costs apply. For urgent legal/enterprise cases we can escalate to infra and prioritize.
sam: For our internal runbook — if we need a faster correlation, use this ES query to include trace/span: 
```
service:model-server AND (request_id:"8d9f3c2a-4b1e-11ee-8f8f-0242ac120002" OR trace_id:"8d9f3c2a-4b1e-11ee-8f8f-0242ac120002")
```
Also check host metrics for GPU memory pressure around that time.
lisa: forwarded to customer. asked for debug bundle link and told them to add header. they replied they can run repro with verbose curl, will send bundle in ~30m. :thumbsup:
maria: thanks all — assigning internal ticket INF-4821 to sam/jon. will update once we get the debug bundle and the customer's verbose curl.
